results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 10.02 defines Conviction to include any admission to or finding of sufficient facts to warrant a finding of guilt, regardless of adjudication, a continuance without a finding, and any plea of guilty or nolo contendere, of or to a crime in any jurisdiction accepted by the court, whether or not a sentence has been imposed. Each feature the pharmacist relies on (dismissal after a CWOF, absence of a sentence, out-of-state forum) is expressly inside the definition, and the same provision makes a conviction conclusive evidence of commission, which disposes of the separate-finding distractor. Key E confirmed.

results.Problem: None. Both keyed propositions and all three rejected propositions were verified individually.
results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) requires report within seven business days of any final action by another governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction, expressly including action against any other health care related professional registration or license held by the registrant, which captures the out-of-state nursing discipline (B). 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) separately requires written report within 30 days of any pending criminal charge or conviction (D). A fails because (aa) is triggered by the charge pending; C fails because (z) is not confined to pharmacy practice; E fails because the two clocks differ in both length and unit. Key B,D confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 10.03(1)(q) makes it a ground for discipline to fail without cause to cooperate with any request by the Board to appear before it or to provide requested information, and separately to fail to respond to a Board subpoena or to furnish records to which the Board is legally entitled. The ground is freestanding and does not depend on the disposition or merit of the underlying complaint, which defeats A, B and D; and it reaches a request as well as a subpoena, which defeats C. Key E confirmed.

(2) describes the advisory letter as an official written document retained in the Board's files that does not constitute formal disciplinary action (A). (3) states that a reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action and that a censure is a severe reprimand (C and D). (4) states that probation consists of a period during which the registrant may practice under conditions imposed by the Board (E). Key A,C,D,E confirmed.

The stem stipulates the conduct is lawful and consistent with good professional practice here, so the conduct-equivalence predicate fails. B, C and D each treat the sister-state action as sufficient or attach a condition the regulation does not impose; E is wrong because the Board is not territorially confined. Key A confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 10.03(3) operates notwithstanding the grounds for discipline specified in 247 CMR 10.03, and provides that no licensee shall be subject to discipline for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services, or for any conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from such services, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice here. Both qualifiers are stipulated, and the sanction arises solely from the protected service, so the carve-out displaces the out-of-state ground rather than competing with it. A, B, C and D each preserve some form of Board action and are foreclosed by the notwithstanding clause. Key E confirmed.

results.Problem: None as to the key. Advisory only: the canonical core reasoning also invokes the limb of 247 CMR 10.03(1) that reaches knowingly permitting an unlicensed person to perform licensed activities, which fits imperfectly here because the technician is licensed. The keyed choice text tracks the authorized-scope limb, and 247 CMR 10.03(1)(f), 9.04(1) and 9.01(10) independently sustain the exposure, so the key and the choice analysis are unaffected.
results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) closes final dispensing process validation to a pharmacy technician, and 247 CMR 9.04(1) assigns that validation to the licensed pharmacist. 247 CMR 10.03(1)(f) makes conduct beyond the authorized scope of a pharmacist, intern or technician a ground for discipline, and 247 CMR 9.01(10) bars a licensee from aiding or abetting the unlawful practice of pharmacy, so the pharmacist who knowingly permits the arrangement is exposed on his own account. Absence of harm (A), the technician's licence (B), documentation (C) and the sequence of Board action against the technician (D) are none of them elements of the ground. Key E confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 8.01(12) requires Massachusetts approved colleges and schools of pharmacy to submit to the Board a written description of each demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program for which internship credit is desired, and provides that the Board may determine whether student participation may be credited toward the internship requirement. Both limbs appear only in A. Clinical pharmacy being an eligible area under 247 CMR 8.01(1)(a)2.a. does not by itself make a given program creditable (B); the duty sits on the school rather than each student (C); separate ACPE accreditation is not the mechanism (D); and preceptor certification does not displace the Board's determination (E). Key A confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 3.01(3)(c) requires a completed examination application to include a certified birth certificate or other sufficient proof of place and date of birth; 247 CMR 3.01(8) permits the Board to refuse to consider an application that has not been properly completed; and 247 CMR 3.01(9) makes all fees submitted in connection with an application reviewed and acted upon by the Board non-refundable. results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.18(4) requires counseling on each new drug therapy and on each drug therapy that in the pharmacist's professional judgment is deemed significant for the health and safety of the patient. The second limb is independent of refill status, so A, B and C fail on their shared premise, and it is calibrated to professional judgment rather than applying to every refill without exception, so D overstates the duty. 247 CMR 9.17(1)(i) reinforces the point by requiring prospective drug utilization review to identify any significant change in drug, dose or directions. Key E confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.18(5) enumerates the information a pharmacist or intern may provide as professional judgment requires, including special directions and instructions for preparation, administration and use by the patient (B), techniques for self-monitoring drug therapy (C), proper storage and disposal (D), and action to be taken in the event of a missed dose or adverse reaction (E). The pharmacy's wholesale acquisition cost is not among the enumerated items, so A is correctly excluded. Key B,C,D,E confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.18(6) requires a designated patient consultation area with Patient Consultation Area signage designed to provide adequate privacy for confidential visual and auditory counseling, and separately requires that the private consultation area be accessible by a patient from the outside of the prescription dispensing area without having to traverse a stockroom or the prescription dispensing area. The stem satisfies the privacy limb but fails the access limb, so A is insufficient and B and C offer cures the provision does not recognise. D misstates the rule, which prescribes an access route rather than a location outside the pharmacy department. Key E confirmed.

A fails because a single entrance sign does not satisfy the adjacent-to-each-area requirement, B fails because the letter height is prescribed, and E fails because the provision prescribes wording rather than a bilingual sign. results.Problem: None as to legal correctness of the key. Disclosure required by the blind protocol: this is the one item of 33 where my Phase-1 blind answer (A, C, E) differs from the canonical key (A, C, D, E). I recorded the ambiguity in the immutable lock before unseal. On verification the canonical key is correct, because 247 CMR 9.15(2) conjunctively requires the pharmacist to determine all four matters and a prescriber's telephone confirmation is evidence going to determination (c) rather than a dispensation from making it. The residual defect is one of item construction rather than law and is carried in the realism record: see the realism review for MA-Q-0288.
results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.15(2) bars a pharmacist from filling a prescription unless the pharmacist, in the exercise of professional judgment, determines that the prescription was issued for a legitimate medical purpose by a practitioner acting in the usual course of professional practice (A), that there is a valid patient-practitioner relationship (C), that the prescription is authentic (D), and that the dispensing is in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19(a) (E). The list is conjunctive and admits no exception where the prescriber confirms authorship; the call is the evidence on which the authenticity determination is made, and the pharmacist retains it as his own professional judgment, which is why D remains keyed. B states no regulatory determination and is correctly excluded. Key A,C,D,E confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.15(1) requires a pharmacist who dispenses medications reported to the Massachusetts Prescription Monitoring Program to register with, and maintain login information for, the electronic system authorized by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A, known as PMP or MassPAT. The duty runs to the individual pharmacist and includes maintenance of the login rather than a single enrolment, so a pharmacy-level account does not discharge it (B). The trigger is dispensing medications reported to the program rather than Schedule II alone (C), and neither disciplinary contact (D) nor delegation by the Manager of Record (E) is a condition. Key A confirmed.

authorities.authority: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, Code of Massachusetts Regulations

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.01(11) bars a licensee from offering, soliciting or receiving remuneration or anything of value to or from any person who owns, operates, manages or is an employee of a hospital, nursing home or other health care facility in return for a referral or for the generation of business from the sale or furnishing of drugs, devices or services. Free catering is a thing of value, the administrator manages a nursing home, and the object is generation of business, so the generation-of-business limb applies without any named patient (A) and without a money payment (B). No disclosure cure (C) or de minimis or budget-based exception (D) appears in the provision. Key E confirmed.

authorities.authority: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, Code of Massachusetts Regulations

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.01(13) provides that, unless otherwise permitted by law, a pharmacist connected with or employed by a hospital or clinic pharmacy that does not hold a Drug Store pharmacy license may not dispense drugs to any person other than inpatients or outpatients of the hospital or clinic, employees of that institution, or those employees' spouses and children who live in the same household. An adult sibling living across town falls outside every permitted class. The family limb is confined to spouses and children in the same household (B), the prescriber's identity does not enlarge the class (C), payment is irrelevant (D), and the restriction reaches drugs generally rather than controlled substances only (E). Key A confirmed.

results.Problem: None. The general qualification list and the prescriptive-practice overlay were separated and checked against both the regulation and the enabling statute.
results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) attaches three conditions where prescriptive practices are included in the agreement: maintaining a current Department-issued controlled substance registration during the term (B); completing the training required by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e); and submitting a MassHealth participation attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury (D). A is wrong twice over, because 247 CMR 16.02(1)(b) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b) set the figure at $1,000,000 per occurrence and because that requirement applies to every agreement rather than only to prescriptive ones. C is wrong twice over for the same reasons, the figure under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e) being five additional contact hours each year. E is wrong because no separate Board licence category exists for collaborating pharmacists. Key B,D confirmed.

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 16.02(2) requires an authorized pharmacist participating in collaborative drug therapy management to maintain evidence of completion of required continuing education for at least two years after the date of the current collaborative practice agreement. The clock therefore runs from the agreement date rather than the course date (A) or the registration renewal (B), the period is two years rather than the life of the licence (D), and the duty is retention rather than transmission to supervising physicians (E), which is a separate duty triggered by discipline under 247 CMR 16.02(3). With an agreement signed six months ago the documentation remains within the retention period. Key C confirmed.

authorities.authority: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, Code of Massachusetts Regulations

results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 16.02(3) provides that whenever an authorized pharmacist participating in collaborative drug therapy management is disciplined by the Board, whether by agreement or Board order, or is otherwise subject to any practice restrictions, the pharmacist must provide written notification of that discipline or practice restriction to each supervising physician. A consent agreement is expressly within the trigger, defeating A; the notice runs to each supervising physician rather than a selected one, defeating B; the notice runs to the physicians rather than the Board, defeating C; and the regulation imposes a notification duty rather than automatic suspension of collaborative practice, defeating E. Key D confirmed.
